claude-bridge/claude-opus-5-5.character: Advisory: Use Opus 5.5 at high for the advisor's own session, including planning and synthesis. Use medium as the economical executor for locked execution packets, mechanical chores, routine checks, repair verification, test-harness findings, focused browser verification, and alternate review. Own investigation, local planning, code choices, and verification within the assignment. For locked packets, use fixed material decisions and deterministic anchors; resolve tooling obstacles locally and escalate material ambiguity outside the assignment. Shares the Anthropic session allowance; at capacity, the advisor session falls back to Grok at high.

cursor/grok-4.6.character: Advisory: The hefty decision-bearing cycle: implementation workhorse and adversarial-tier checker. Backend, data, mixed-stack, substantial existing-UX, greenfield UX (load frontend-design), research, schema/auth/security/money checks, final whole-diff review, and rechecks after an overturned pass. Own investigation, planning, implementation or repair, and verification within the assignment. Prefer Opus 5.5 medium when material decisions are already locked. Grok is also the advisor fallback when Opus 5.5 is at capacity, including planning and synthesis. 200K window — keep packets task-shaped and split oversized reviews per package or phase. Review a Grok build in a fresh Grok context when useful; independence means a nonauthor assessment, not a different model. This guide recommends Cursor only as cursor/grok-4.6. Preserve Cursor catalog fast-mode default.
